name: Kong API Gateway
description: Protects against destructive Kong Gateway CLI, deck CLI, and Admin API \ operations.

destructive_patterns.name: deck-reset
destructive_patterns.description: deck reset removes ALL Kong configuration. This is extremely dangerous and irreversible.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
Resetting Kong removes ALL services, routes, plugins, consumers, certificates, and \ upstreams. Your entire API gateway configuration is wiped. All traffic through Kong \ will fail immediately. There is no undo.

\ Safer alternatives: \ - deck dump: Export current configuration first \ - deck diff: Review what will change before any sync \ - Delete specific entities instead of full reset

destructive_patterns.name: deck-sync-destructive
destructive_patterns.description: deck sync with --select-tag can remove entities not matching the tag.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
Using --select-tag with deck sync removes entities not matching the tag in your \ state file. This can accidentally delete services and routes managed by other teams \ or systems. Entities without tags are at risk of deletion.

\ Safer alternatives: \ - deck diff --select-tag: Preview changes first \ - Use consistent tagging across all entities \ - Consider deck sync without --select-tag to avoid surprises

destructive_patterns.name: kong-admin-delete-services
destructive_patterns.description: DELETE request to Kong Admin API removes services.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
Deleting a Kong service removes the upstream service definition. All routes \ associated with the service become orphaned and stop working. Traffic to those \ endpoints will return 404 errors.

\ Safer alternatives: \ - GET /services first: List services to verify the target \ - Delete routes pointing to the service first \ - Use deck dump to export configuration before changes

destructive_patterns.name: kong-admin-delete-routes
destructive_patterns.description: DELETE request to Kong Admin API removes routes.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
Deleting a Kong route removes the path-to-service mapping. Requests to that path \ will return 404 errors. Plugins attached to the route are also removed. The \ associated service is not affected.

\ Safer alternatives: \ - GET /routes first: Verify the route details \ - Test in a non-production environment \ - Consider disabling plugins instead of deleting the route

destructive_patterns.name: kong-admin-delete-plugins
destructive_patterns.description: DELETE request to Kong Admin API removes plugins.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
Deleting a Kong plugin removes its functionality from the associated service, route, \ or consumer. Authentication, rate limiting, logging, or transformation features \ provided by the plugin stop immediately.

\ Safer alternatives: \ - GET /plugins first: Review plugin configuration \ - PATCH to disable the plugin instead of deleting \ - Export plugin config with deck dump before deletion

destructive_patterns.name: kong-admin-delete-consumers
destructive_patterns.description: DELETE request to Kong Admin API removes consumers.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
Deleting a Kong consumer removes the API client identity. All credentials (API keys, \ JWT, OAuth) for that consumer are revoked. Plugins configured per-consumer stop \ applying. Affected clients lose API access.

\ Safer alternatives: \ - GET /consumers first: Review consumer details \ - Delete individual credentials instead of the consumer \ - Notify affected clients before deletion

destructive_patterns.name: kong-admin-delete-upstreams
destructive_patterns.description: DELETE request to Kong Admin API removes upstreams.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
Deleting a Kong upstream removes the load balancer and all its targets. Services \ using this upstream will fail to route traffic. Health checks and circuit breaker \ settings are lost.

\ Safer alternatives: \ - GET /upstreams first: Review upstream configuration \ - Update services to use a different upstream first \ - Remove targets individually to verify impact

destructive_patterns.name: kong-admin-delete-targets
destructive_patterns.description: DELETE request to Kong Admin API removes targets.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
Deleting a Kong target removes a backend server from the upstream pool. Traffic \ is redistributed to remaining targets. If this was the last target, the upstream \ has no backends and requests fail.

\ Safer alternatives: \ - GET /upstreams/{id}/targets first: List current targets \ - Set target weight to 0 to drain traffic first \ - Verify other targets can handle the load

destructive_patterns.name: kong-admin-delete-certificates
destructive_patterns.description: DELETE request to Kong Admin API removes certificates.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
Deleting a Kong certificate removes the TLS/SSL certificate. SNIs using this \ certificate will fail TLS handshakes. HTTPS traffic to affected domains will \ receive certificate errors.

\ Safer alternatives: \ - GET /certificates first: Review certificate details \ - Upload a replacement certificate before deletion \ - Remove associated SNIs first

destructive_patterns.name: kong-admin-delete-snis
destructive_patterns.description: DELETE request to Kong Admin API removes SNIs.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
Deleting a Kong SNI removes the domain-to-certificate mapping. HTTPS requests \ for that hostname will fail TLS negotiation or use a default certificate if \ configured. Clients will see certificate warnings.

\ Safer alternatives: \ - GET /snis first: Review SNI configuration \ - Update the SNI to point to a different certificate \ - Verify the certificate is no longer needed for this domain

destructive_patterns.name: kong-admin-delete-generic
destructive_patterns.description: DELETE request to Kong Admin API can remove configuration.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
DELETE requests to the Kong Admin API remove configuration objects. The specific \ impact depends on the endpoint: services, routes, plugins, consumers, certificates, \ or other Kong entities. Deletions take effect immediately.

\ Safer alternatives: \ - Use GET requests first to review the resource \ - Export configuration with deck dump \ - Test changes in a staging environment
